reference_opening.argument: This video is scam content because it promotes a cryptocurrency earning system with unusually large income claims, a BUSD registration requirement, and earnings described as depending on referrals, partner positions, and recycled or upgraded slots. It reinforces the promotion with displayed earning figures and directions to contact or join through supplied channels, while the separate target, crypto-signals graphic, and lead-generation course are presented as additional benefits without established performance or transaction outcomes.

opening.argument: The presentation includes material risk language and conditions that are inconsistent with a deceptive guarantee. It expressly warns that trading can produce losses without sufficient knowledge, and says profit depends on taking action, learning, and working hard. The crypto-signals material also emphasizes analysis rather than forecasting. These qualifications frame the offering as conditional and risk-bearing financial commentary, not a promise that every viewer will earn money.

citations.quote: you should know that in every trading if you don't have knowledge then you will loose there
but you'll have to take a step start system and learn and to work hard so you'll be able to make a profit

rebuttal.rebuttal: The cited registration and referral explanations show disclosed terms, not deception. Saying that a participant can earn after referring three people describes a condition of the program; it does not establish that returns are guaranteed. Likewise, “win to win” is promotional characterization, but the presentation separately acknowledges possible trading losses and the need for knowledge.

citations.quote: Here the registration amount is ten BOSD. with ten BUSD, you will start this system.

if you don't have it then what would happen if you loose

true_side_reply.rebuttal: A risk warning about trading does not qualify the separate earning structure being promoted. The video says income is tied to referring people, sponsor and cross-line positions, and repeatedly upgrading slots. The work-hard language is a general condition, while the speaker also presents a one-lakh monthly target and invites viewers to join for it. Those qualifications do not show that the advertised matrix produces ordinary investment returns.

opening.argument: The video's dominant activity is explaining how named programs operate. It walks through X3 and X4 circles, slots, placement, recycling, and payment flows, while the supplied slides visually present diagrams and tables labeled for those programs. The speaker repeatedly introduces the material as something viewers will understand and learn. That is consistent with an operational demonstration or business-education presentation; explaining an earning model does not by itself prove that the presenter is certifying every outcome.

citations.quote: In which we will know how they do generate passive and pure income and how is it different from the network marketing And affiliate marketing
Now lets understand how the rest of the earnings are distributed

rebuttal.rebuttal: The instructional format does not change the subject being taught. The explanation repeatedly connects payment to referrals, sponsors, team members, and slot upgrades, and calls viewers to join a team. A tutorial can still be promotional when its lesson is how to enter and profit from the presented system.

citations.quote: if you referred 3 people first circle you get earning on third circle then you will get the earning
when you upgrade your slots, you get to multiply more earnings

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The diagrams are not neutral technical documentation. The speaker uses them to explain how viewers can earn, upgrade, and obtain unlimited money, then directs interested viewers to contact him and join his team. The educational presentation therefore teaches participation in the same recruitment-based structure rather than merely analyzing it from a distance.

citations.quote: After upgrading, you are eligible to earn unlimited money
then we will work together so friends, hope everything will be clear to you

opening.argument: The material can be read as promotion of a bundled set of ordinary services and training: trading signals, a lead-generation course, job-finding instruction, and personal mentorship. The signals are expressly described as analysis rather than forecasting, and the course is separately presented as Lead Generation Mastery. The supplied material does not show a request for passwords, identity documents, or other credentials, nor does it establish an actual payment outcome. That supports treating this as a disclosed service and educational offer rather than inferring a scam from promotional language alone.

citations.quote: We provide you with signals from a expert
will get a course organic life generation because this business belongs to all
For Personal Mentorship and more information Contact 8825143458 (Whatsapp/Call)

rebuttal.rebuttal: The additional services do not displace the core offer. The same presentation requires an initial BUSD amount, explains earnings through circles and sponsors, and promotes team membership. A lack of credential collection is not decisive when the described mechanism instead centers on financial entry, placement, and recycling.

citations.quote: with ten BUSD, you will start this system.
For the sponsors and for cross lines everyone gets profit.
when you upgrade your slots, you get to multiply more earnings

true_side_reply.rebuttal: Calling signals and courses bundled services does not account for the principal earning mechanism. The video describes a paid BUSD entry, referral-dependent circles, sponsor and cross-line payments, and repeated slot upgrades. It also markets a specific monthly target and invites direct contact, so the absence of password requests or proven payouts does not make the recruitment structure ordinary commerce.
